subject: dispute on an already-refunded order
body: A customer just filed a dispute on an order we had ALREADY fully refunded three weeks ago (refund_8_01, well before any dispute existed). Do we still need to respond with evidence, or does the existing refund automatically settle it in our favor? Not sure how this even works when it's the refund that came first.
evidence_gap_fact: corpus/policy/refund-timelines.md's 'Refunds and dispute status' section only covers the forward case (a refund issued while a dispute is already open); neither it nor corpus/policy/chargebacks-disputes.md addresses the reverse sequence (a dispute opened on a transaction already refunded beforehand). merchant_8's fixture has no dispute record to consult either — disputes is empty.

subject: changing settlement bank account
body: We're switching our current account to a different bank next month. How do I update the bank account linked for settlement payouts on my account, and roughly how long does the change take to go live?
evidence_gap_fact: No policy document describes a procedure or timeline for changing the bank account linked to settlement. corpus/policy/settlement-cycles.md only states that funds are 'settled to the merchant's linked bank account' as a given, never how to change it. merchant_1's fixture has no bank-account field at all.

subject: GST on platform fees
body: Noticed an extra GST line on our platform fee invoice this month that wasn't there before - did the tax rate on processing fees change recently, or is this specific to us somehow?
evidence_gap_fact: No policy document mentions taxation, GST, or any fee/invoicing schedule for platform processing fees. The only 'GST' mention anywhere in the KB is in corpus/policy/kyc-documents.md, referring to a GST registration certificate as a KYC document — unrelated to tax on fees. No merchant fixture has a fees or tax field.

subject: PCI compliance certificate needed
body: Our new logistics partner is asking us for proof of PCI-DSS compliance from our payment processor before they'll integrate with us. Can someone send over a compliance certificate or point me to where I can get one?
evidence_gap_fact: No policy document mentions PCI-DSS, security compliance certification, or any process for issuing compliance documentation to a merchant. Not covered anywhere in the KB or in merchant_9's fixture.

subject: in-store card machine error
body: We just opened a small physical counter alongside our online store. Our card machine for in-person payments is showing an error at checkout - is this something you all handle too or is that a completely different system?
evidence_gap_fact: The entire policy KB and every merchant fixture describe only online gateway transactions (card/UPI/netbanking/wallet at checkout); there is no mention anywhere of physical POS terminals, offline card machines, or an offline-acceptance process.

subject: reserve if we close the account
body: Hypothetically - if we ever decided to shut Trailblazer down entirely, what happens to the amount currently sitting in our reserve? Does it just get forfeited, or does it still get released to us on the original schedule even after the account is closed?
evidence_gap_fact: No policy document describes an account-closure or deactivation procedure at all. corpus/policy/rolling-reserves.md's 'Reserve removal' section covers only early removal via a risk-team review after the trigger resolves - it says nothing about what happens to a held balance on account closure.

subject: combining two subscriptions
body: One of our customers has two separate subscriptions with us (a course plan and an exam-prep add-on, each its own mandate). She wants us to combine them into a single monthly mandate/charge instead of two separate ones. Is that something we can do on our end, or does the platform not support merging mandates like that?
evidence_gap_fact: corpus/policy/subscription-mandates.md describes only a single mandate's lifecycle (registration, retries, cancellation, amount changes via a new mandate); it never addresses combining or merging two separate active mandates for the same customer.

subject: evidence for unauthorized transaction disputes
body: Before it comes up for real - if a customer ever disputes a transaction as 'unauthorized', is there anything specific we should have on file beyond the usual delivery proof and order confirmation? Wondering if something like an OTP/authentication record matters more for that particular kind of claim.
evidence_gap_fact: corpus/policy/chargebacks-disputes.md's 'What counts as sufficient evidence' section only special-cases the 'product not as described' reason code; it never specifies additional or different evidence requirements for an 'unauthorized_transaction' claim specifically.

identity_note: Third-party relay message (an accountant managing multiple clients) with no merchant id and no business name given yet - genuinely unresolvable until the sender provides identifying details, and even then identity should be verified before disclosing account information to a third party.
